thread:
jordan: Hey team — ACME reported a sudden p99 jump for their API calls around 14:12 UTC, pegging at ~2.1s (normal ~350ms). They say it started after we pushed the small-batcher tweak yesterday. Details: tenant=acme-corp, route=/v1/generate, region=us-west-2.

maya: Thanks — can you paste the customer request pattern? small prompts or long? any rate change?

jordan: Mostly small prompts, average prompt tokens ~12, peak qps unchanged. Uploading sample trace and logs: https://internal-logs/redwood/trace/abcd1234 :eyes:

opsbot: Deploy completed: commit 9f7a2b9 (eng-sre/batching) at 2025-06-03T13:05:00Z.

lee: I pulled the trace — I see a pattern where requests hit the continuous-batcher and wait an extra linger window before flush. There are repeated cycles: batch fills then long tail waits (~1.7s extra). Looks like the configured min_batch_size=8 and linger_ms=1200 combined with adaptive-coalesce off.

sam: Is this the same customer that hit p95 regressions last quarter? (tenant id matches) If so we had a custom route config for them.

jordan: Yes same tenant. They had a custom batch_policy applied via tenant-configs yesterday: {
```
route: /v1/generate
continuous_batching:
  min_batch_size: 8
  linger_ms: 1200
  max_batch_size: 64
  adaptive_coalesce: false
```
}

maya: That linger_ms looks high for tiny prompts. With min_batch_size 8 we wait up to 1.2s if batch doesn't fill — explains p99 spikes. But why did it regress now? We rolled a tweak to batching priority that deprioritized tiny requests (to help throughput). That change made tiny requests more likely to hit the linger timeout instead of being greedily coalesced.

lee: Repro steps I used in staging: spin up 10 clients at 10 rps each with prompt size 12 tokens, set tenant config above, run for 20m. Observed p99 ~2s and p50 ~300ms. Curl sample to repro quickly:
```
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://staging.redwood/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":8}' &
  sleep 0.05
done
```
You can see the batching logs: `BATCHER_WAIT linger_ms=1200 size=3 waited=1187ms` repeated.

sam: Good repro. Can we confirm this is not an auth/billing flap? I checked billing and auth — no errors. Only latency.

maya: Mitigation options:
- immediate hotfix: lower linger_ms to 100 (customer-level override) -> removes the 1.2s tail.
- medium: enable adaptive_coalesce so tiny requests are more likely to be coalesced quickly.
- long-term: implement dynamic linger per prompt-size distribution.

jordan: Customer requested quick fix. Can we do tenant override now?

lee: I can push a tenant override to reduce linger_ms to 80 and min_batch_size to 4. Will do a canary (1% of their traffic) and watch p99.

opsbot: Change request queued: tenant-config-update acme-corp {linger_ms:80, min_batch_size:4} by lee. Change ID 9812.

maya: After the canary we should also run the staging repro with adaptive_coalesce=true to measure throughput/cost impact. If stable, roll to prod.

lee: Canary results after 10m: p99 dropped from 2.1s -> 360ms for the canary slice. No errors, CPU/GPU utilization unchanged.

jordan: Customer confirmed improved latency on their end. They asked whether this will increase token cost.

sam: Lower linger reduces batching efficiency, so unit cost might rise slightly for small prompts. We'll quantify. Maya, can Optimize run an estimate?

maya: Will run Optimize offline and post numbers. For now propose: keep override at tenant level, schedule adapt_coalesce trial next week, and add alert for linger_ms > 300ms on tiny-prompt routes.

lee: Filed follow-up task: ENG-4268 "automatic per-tenant linger tuning + alert".

jordan: Thanks all. Closing escalation once Optimize numbers are back and customer signs off. :thumbsup:
